subject: Digital Logic
chapters: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Logic Gates
Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
Chapter 6: Memory and Programmable Logic Devices

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Logic Gates
questions.text:
Explain Number Systems (Binary, Octal, Decimal, Hexadecimal) and Radix Conversion. Perform base conversions:
(a) $(1011011.101)_2 = (?)_{10} = (?)_{16}$,
(b) $(735.25)_8 = (?)_{16} = (?)_{2}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Logic Gates
questions.text:
Explain Signed Binary Representations: Signed-Magnitude, 1's Complement, and 2's Complement. Perform binary arithmetic using 2's complement (8-bit system):
(a) $(+28)_{10} - (+15)_{10}$,
(b) $(-35)_{10} - (+42)_{10}$. Detect whether overflow occurred.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Logic Gates
questions.text: Perform binary subtraction using 1's complement and 2's complement methods: $(11010)_2 - (10111)_2$ and $(1001)_2 - (11010)_2$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Logic Gates
questions.text: Explain Binary Codes: BCD (8421 code), Excess-3 code, Gray code, and ASCII. Why is Gray code called a unit-distance code? Convert $(110101)_{\text{Gray}}$ to binary and $(101101)_2$ to Gray code.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Number Systems and Logic Gates
questions.text: Explain Error Detection and Correction Codes: Even/Odd Parity bit scheme and Hamming (7, 4) Code. Generate Hamming code for data word `1011` and correct a single-bit error in received word `1010101`.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
questions.text: State and prove De Morgan's Theorems algebraically and using truth tables. Why are NAND and NOR called Universal Gates? Realize AND, OR, and NOT operations using NAND gates only.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
questions.text: Simplify the Boolean function using Boolean algebra theorems and verify using truth table: $F = A B + A(B+C) + B(B+C)$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
questions.text:
Simplify the 4-variable Boolean function using Karnaugh Map (K-Map) in SOP and POS forms with Don't Care conditions:
$F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 15) + d(3, 11, 13)$. Realize the simplified function using minimum NAND gates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
questions.text: Simplify 4-variable POS function using K-Map: $F(A, B, C, D) = \prod M(1, 3, 5, 7, 13, 15) \cdot d(8, 9, 10, 11)$ and realize using minimum NOR gates.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
questions.text: Simplify the Boolean function using Quine-McCluskey (Tabular) Method: $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(1, 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15)$. Identify all Prime Implicants (PI) and Essential Prime Implicants (EPI).

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Boolean Algebra and Simplification Techniques
questions.text: Simplify using Tabular Method with Don't care terms: $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(0, 1, 2, 8, 9) + d(10, 11, 14, 15)$.
Design a Half Adder and Full Adder circuit using truth table, K-Map simplification, and logic gates. Realize a Full Adder using two Half Adders and one OR gate.
Design a Half Subtractor and Full Subtractor circuit using logic gates. Show how a full subtractor can be constructed using two half subtractors.

Design a 4-bit Binary Parallel Adder/Subtractor circuit using 4 Full Adders and XOR gates with control signal $M$ ($M=0$ for addition, $M=1$ for subtraction). Explain carry propagation delay and Carry Look-Ahead (CLA) generator.
Design a BCD (Decimal) Adder circuit using two 4-bit binary adders (IC 7483) and correction logic for sum $> 9$ or carry out.
Design a BCD (8421) to Excess-3 Code Converter and Binary to Gray code converter using K-Maps and basic logic gates.
Design a 3-to-8 line Decoder with Enable input. Implement full adder logic using a 3-to-8 decoder and external OR gates.
Design a 4-to-2 Priority Encoder with active-low inputs/outputs and valid output indicator $V$.

What is a Multiplexer (Data Selector)? Design an 8-to-1 MUX using truth table and logic gates. Implement the Boolean function $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(1, 3, 4, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15)$ using an 8-to-1 Multiplexer.
Implement the Boolean function $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(0, 1, 3, 4, 8, 9, 15)$ using a 4-to-1 Multiplexer and external logic.
Design a 1-to-8 Demultiplexer (DEMUX) and explain its relationship with a Decoder.
Design a 2-bit Magnitude Comparator that compares two 2-bit binary numbers $A(A_1 A_0)$ and $B(B_1 B_0)$ and generates outputs $A > B, A = B, A < B$.

Explain Latches vs Flip-Flops (Level-triggered vs Edge-triggered). Explain SR Latch, Gated SR Latch, and D Flip-Flop. Explain the Race-Around Condition in JK Flip-Flop and how Master-Slave JK Flip-Flop eliminates it.
Explain Characteristic Tables, Characteristic Equations, and Excitation Tables for SR, JK, D, and T flip-flops. Convert a JK Flip-Flop into a D Flip-Flop and T Flip-Flop.
Convert an SR Flip-Flop into a JK Flip-Flop showing conversion table, K-Maps, and logic diagram.
Design a Synchronous 3-bit Up/Down Counter using JK Flip-Flops with state diagram, state table, K-Map excitation simplification, and complete circuit diagram.
Design a Mod-6 (or Mod-10 BCD Decade) Synchronous Counter using T Flip-Flops showing state diagram, excitation table, K-Maps, and unused state lockup check.
Design an Asynchronous (Ripple) 3-bit Up/Down Counter using negative edge-triggered JK flip-flops.

Explain Shift Registers: SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO. Design a 4-bit Universal Shift Register using D flip-flops and 4-to-1 multiplexers with mode control inputs ($S_1 S_0$: Hold, Shift Right, Shift Left, Parallel Load). Explain Ring Counter and Johnson (Twisted Ring) Counter.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Memory and Programmable Logic Devices
questions.text: Explain Programmable Logic Devices (PLDs): Read Only Memory (ROM), Programmable Logic Array (PLA: Programmable AND, Programmable OR), and Programmable Array Logic (PAL: Programmable AND, Fixed OR). Implement functions $F_1 = \sum m(0, 1, 3, 5)$ and $F_2 = \sum m(1, 2, 4, 7)$ using PLA.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Memory and Programmable Logic Devices
questions.text: Implement a Full Adder and Full Subtractor circuit using PAL with fixed OR gates.

Compare Logic Families: TTL (Transistor-Transistor Logic), CMOS (Complementary MOS), and ECL (Emitter Coupled Logic) in terms of Propagation Delay, Power Dissipation, Fan-In, Fan-Out, and Noise Margin.
Explain TTL NAND Gate with Totem-Pole output stage, Open-Collector output, and Tristate output logic.
Explain Hardware Description Language (VHDL/Verilog): Entity and Architecture declarations. Write VHDL/Verilog code for a 4-to-1 Multiplexer and Full Adder.
